input.candidate_text:
Assume for contradiction that \(x>1\). Taking \(n=2\), since \(\varphi(2)=1\), gives
\[
4y^2+1\mid x-1.
\]
Choose a prime \(p\mid 4y^2+1\). Then \(p\) is odd, \(p\nmid y\), and \((2y)^2\equiv-1\pmod p\), so \(p\equiv1\pmod4\). In particular, \(p\mid x-1\). Put
\[
s=v_p(x-1),\qquad K=s+1.
\]

We construct a positive integer \(n\) such that
\[
p^K\mid n^2y^2+1\quad\text{and}\quad p\nmid\varphi(n).
\]
Let \(f(T)=y^2T^2+1\). We have \(f(2)\equiv0\pmod p\) and
\[
f'(2)=4y^2\not\equiv0\pmod p.
\]
Hence Hensel lifting gives a unit \(r\pmod{p^K}\), with \(r\equiv2\pmod p\), such that \(f(r)\equiv0\pmod{p^K}\).

We also need a convenient representative of this residue class. Choose a primitive root \(g\) modulo \(p\). One of \(g\) and \(g+p\) is a primitive root modulo \(p^2\): if \(g^{p-1}\equiv1\pmod{p^2}\), then
\[
(g+p)^{p-1}\equiv g^{p-1}+(p-1)g^{p-2}p\not\equiv1\pmod{p^2}.
\]
Call the resulting integer \(a\). It is a primitive root modulo every \(p^j\): indeed, \(v_p(a^{p-1}-1)=1\), so LTE gives
\[
v_p\bigl(a^{(p-1)m}-1\bigr)=1+v_p(m).
\]
Moreover, \(1<a<2p\), \(p\nmid a\), and \(a\not\equiv1\pmod p\). The prime-factor formula for \(\varphi(a)\) then shows \(p\nmid\varphi(a)\): otherwise some prime divisor \(q\mid a\) would satisfy \(q\equiv1\pmod p\); since \(q\le a<2p\), this would force \(q=a\equiv1\pmod p\), a contradiction.

Because \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p^K\), choose \(e\ge1\) such that \(a^e\equiv r\pmod{p^K}\), and set \(n=a^e\). Then
\[
p^K\mid n^2y^2+1,
\]
while
\[
\varphi(n)=\varphi(a^e)=a^{e-1}\varphi(a)
\]
is not divisible by \(p\).

Applying the hypothesis to this \(n\) yields
\[
p^K\mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1.
\]
However, because \(p\) is odd, \(p\mid x-1\), and \(p\nmid\varphi(n)\), LTE gives
\[
v_p\bigl(x^{\varphi(n)}-1\bigr)
=v_p(x-1)+v_p(\varphi(n))=s<K,
\]
a contradiction. Thus \(x>1\) is impossible. Since \(x\) is a positive integer, \(x=1\).

problem.theorem:
Let \( x \) and \( y \) be positive integers. If for each positive integer \( n \) we have that

\[
(n y)^{2}+1 \mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1
\]

prove that \( x=1 \).
